Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh we know schedules are tight so we wanted to get a quick kickoff to align on the onboarding runway and what you need from us.
[00:12] Samir Patel: yeah thanks Maya, appreciate it. we, um, we ran the trial and it looks promising. main thing now is to understand network and data handling. Diego is on to talk infra.
[00:24] Diego Marquez: hey, yeah hi. main constraint for us is that our legal team wants isolate data within our VPC and they want KMS integration. we also are interested in predictable latency for customer-facing flows.
[00:38] Alex Rivera: got it. so two big threads: private VPC/KMS and latency/throughput SLOs. we'll unpack both. brief question — are you planning persistent Dedicated capacity or a private deployment behind your VPC?
[00:52] Laura Kim: leaning toward a private VPC managed deployment initially, but we might buy reserved/dedicated for peak hours. we need to figure out autoscale and cost model.
[01:05] Maya Chen: perfect. we'll include both patterns in the runbook and a decision matrix — when to use Dedicated vs private on-prem-like setups.
[01:16] Samir Patel: also — for perf benchmarks we need to know what the baseline numbers are. the trial used small batches and got 250ms median but worse p95; baseline for us is p95 < 800ms on 2k qps.
[01:29] Alex Rivera: okay interesting. couple clarifying things: is that 2k qps concurrently or bursts per second? and what's average sequence length?
[01:36] Samir Patel: average seq length about 200 tokens; we have bursts — like 3k for short periods.
[01:45] Alex Rivera: ok that helps. we'll propose a perf test plan that simulates your burst profile and sequence distribution.
[01:53] Diego Marquez: on security, can you confirm SOC2 and SSO support? our compliance team asked for audit logs and SSO via SAML.
[02:03] Maya Chen: yes — we support SSO SAML, RBAC, and can export audit logs. for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping — we'll send the security pack that outlines the exact flow.
[02:18] Laura Kim: great. can you also note data retention for logs? we usually need 7 years for certain logs, and we need the ability to redact PII before logs leave the environment.
[02:29] Alex Rivera: okay, we'll include redaction patterns and log retention options — but to be clear, for Private deployments most of the logs can stay in your VPC and we only pull metadata if you opt in. there might be small telemetry to our control plane for health checks — we'll make that explicit.
[02:45] Samir Patel: yeah that's the tricky part, we need clarity on the telemetry. need docs.
[02:50] Maya Chen: action item — we'll add a telemetry appendix to the runbook.
[02:55] Diego Marquez: excellent. on network: we need the exact port list and CIDR ranges for peering, and any machine-init steps.
[03:05] Alex Rivera: we'll provide a network checklist + example terraform snippets. for peering we use a small range of egress IPs for control-plane callbacks and a set of health check ports; exacts in the doc.
[03:18] Samir Patel: about pilot timeline: we're aiming for a pilot in mid-April, full rollout by end of Q2. is that realistic?
[03:27] Maya Chen: yes — pilot in six weeks is typical if we get runbook approvals and sample data early. timeline depends on network/infra review.
[03:34] Laura Kim: ok, so what's the minimal data you need for the perf test? do you take sanitized logs or synthetic traffic?
[03:42] Alex Rivera: we can accept sanitized production-like traffic or a synthetic generator that matches token lengths and qps. ideally both: sanitized sample for accuracy regressions, synthetic for load testing.
[03:52] Samir Patel: we'll prioritize sanitized samples + a synthetic traffic generator script.
[03:56] Maya Chen: quick note — we'll also recommend quantization and batching knobs for cost. often customers change batching window and kv cache TTL to hit their p95 targets without overprovisioning.
[04:10] Diego Marquez: does Redwood support on-the-fly model fallbacks if capacity hits? like degrade to smaller model under pressure?
[04:18] Alex Rivera: yes, routing policies can fallback to a compatible smaller variant. we can set automatic fallback thresholds and circuit-breakers. be aware of quality degradation tradeoffs which we'll capture.
[04:30] Samir Patel: good. competitors question — our SRE asked whether you integrate with Pinecone for vector store or do you recommend in-house.
[04:39] Maya Chen: Redwood integrates with many vector stores, Pinecone included; we also have embedding ops recommendations. we'll include a recommended architecture.
[04:48] Laura Kim: teammate question — audit logs: are they stored in our S3 or do they go to Redwood?
[04:56] Alex Rivera: default for Private is that logs stay in customer's S3 and we only store minimal metadata in our control plane if you want managed billing. full details in the security pack.
[05:06] Diego Marquez: ok that's helpful. next steps/recap?
[05:10] Maya Chen: recap: Maya will send runbook + security pack + network checklist by 2026-03-03; Alex will follow up to schedule an infra deep-dive and perf benchmark session for next week (aiming 2026-03-06); VectorGrid will share sanitized traffic samples and redaction rules by 2026-03-05.
[05:28] Samir Patel: sounds good. any blockers on our side? I think legal needs the security pack to move forward.
[05:35] Maya Chen: we'll push the security pack with KMS flow diagrams and SAML SSO details.
[05:41] Laura Kim: one last thing — can you include a rudimentary cost estimate for dedicated vs private? rough order magnitude.
[05:48] Alex Rivera: yes, we'll provide cost-per-1000 tokens and a compare table with expected infra commit ranges. note this is an estimate; we'll refine after perf tests.
[05:58] Diego Marquez: thanks.
[06:00] Maya Chen: thanks team, we'll follow up via email and drop the runbook in the shared folder.
